headings.title: Definition and criteria of home school
headings.reviewNote: Defines home school as an entity providing private or religious instruction to enrolled children without tuition or FPE classification.

headings.title: Mandatory instructional records and hourly requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires parents to maintain plan books, portfolios, and evaluation records, and offer one thousand hours of instruction with six hundred core hours.

headings.title: Exemption for pupils sixteen and older
headings.reviewNote: Exempts pupils sixteen years of age or older from home school instructional record and hourly requirements.

headings.title: Daily log defense and prosecuting attorney review
headings.reviewNote: Makes production of a daily log or, for pupils sixteen or older who attended a metropolitan district the previous year, a written compliance statement a defense to section 167.031 prosecutions and chapter 210 educational neglect actions, with enforcement and records reviewable only by the local prosecuting attorney.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 167.012 governing home school definitions, instructional records and hours, age-sixteen exemption, and daily log defenses.

headings.title: Definition and criteria of FPE school
headings.reviewNote: Defines Family Paced Education (FPE) school providing private or religious-based instruction without tuition and permitted to enroll children participating in sections 135.712 to 135.719 and 166.700 to 166.720 programs without a background check.

headings.title: Mandatory instructional records and hourly requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires maintenance of plan books, work portfolios, and progress evaluations, offering one thousand hours of instruction with six hundred core hours.

headings.title: Exemption for pupils sixteen and older
headings.reviewNote: Exempts pupils sixteen years of age or older from FPE school record and instructional hour requirements.

headings.title: Daily log defense and prosecuting attorney review
headings.reviewNote: Makes production of a daily log or, for pupils sixteen or older who attended a metropolitan district the previous year, a written compliance statement a defense to section 167.031 prosecutions and chapter 210 educational neglect actions, with enforcement and records reviewable only by the local prosecuting attorney.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 167.013 governing Family Paced Education (FPE) school definitions, instructional records and hours, age-sixteen exemption, and daily log defenses.

headings.title: Title of Foster Care Education Bill of Rights
headings.reviewNote: Establishes statutory title as the Foster Care Education Bill of Rights for sections 167.018 and 167.019.

headings.title: Designation and duties of educational liaison
headings.reviewNote: Requires each school district to designate an educational liaison to facilitate placement, enrollment, credit transfers, and records requests.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.018 governing the Foster Care Education Bill of Rights and district educational liaison duties.

headings.title: Placement stability and school of origin attendance
headings.reviewNote: Requires child-placing agencies to consider attendance areas, protecting rights to remain in schools of origin and defining best interest defaults.

headings.title: Mandatory credit acceptance for completed coursework
headings.reviewNote: Requires each school district to accept full or partial coursework satisfactorily completed by a pupil while attending a public, nonpublic, or nonsectarian school in accordance with district policies or regulations.

headings.title: High school diploma issuance by residence district
headings.reviewNote: Requires the school district of residence to issue a diploma to a pupil who completes its graduation requirements while under juvenile court jurisdiction under chapter 211.

headings.title: Protection against grade lowering during placement absences
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits lowering pupil grades or credits due to court-ordered placement changes, appearances, or related proceedings.

headings.title: Agency access to pupil education records
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school districts to permit child-placing agencies access to pupil records for educational case management and transfer assistance.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Subjects rules promulgated under this section to chapter 536 administrative procedures and nonseverability provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 167.019 governing foster pupil placement stability, course credits, graduation diplomas, and agency records access.

headings.title: Definitions of threat assessment, homeless youth, and safety plan
headings.reviewNote: Defines behavioral threat assessment, homeless child or homeless youth, and personal safety plan for sections 167.020 and 167.022.

headings.title: Registration proof options and safety hearing
headings.reviewNote: Requires proof of residency, a waiver request within the last forty-five days, or military relocation orders at registration, and permits a safety hearing within five working days when immediate danger is suspected.

headings.title: Hardship waiver request and hearing procedures
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes board waiver requests for hardship or good cause, barring athletic justifications, and establishes appeal rights to circuit court.

headings.title: Criminal penalty for false registration statements
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowingly submitting false information to satisfy any subsection 2 registration requirement as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Civil recovery of educational costs from parents
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school boards to bring civil actions against parents or guardians submitting false information to recover student attendance costs.

headings.title: Exemptions from standard registration residency requirements
headings.reviewNote: Exempts homeless youth, desegregation transfer students, wards of the state, residential care placements, and alternative program pupils.

headings.title: Mandatory records request and disciplinary disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Requires enrolling officials to request transfer, discipline, threat assessment, and safety plan records within two business days.

headings.title: Remote registration for relocating military families
headings.reviewNote: Allows military families relocating under orders to complete remote registration and submit residency proof within ten days of attendance.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsection headings for 167.020 governing student registration residency proof, hardship waivers, penalties, and military student procedures.

headings.title: State board policy on disciplinary record expungement
headings.reviewNote: Directs the state board of education to adopt policies for expunging disciplinary records of graduated pupils or those reaching age twenty-one.

headings.title: Local school district adoption of expungement policies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes local school districts to adopt disciplinary record expungement policies consistent with state board policy.

headings.title: Expungement prohibition for section 167.115 acts
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits expunging any act listed in subsection 1 of section 167.115 unless the petition was dismissed or the pupil was acquitted or adjudicated not to have committed the act.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.026 governing state and local policies for expunging pupil disciplinary records.

headings.title: Definition of student special education record
headings.reviewNote: Defines student special education record to include individualized education programs, individualized family service plans, and 504 plans.

headings.title: Permanent record status in cumulative scholastic records
headings.reviewNote: Deems student special education records to be permanent records maintained as part of cumulative scholastic records starting in 2023-24.

headings.title: Prohibition on destruction of special education records
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits school districts and public schools from destroying a child's most recent student special education record.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.027 governing the permanent retention and preservation of student special education records.

headings.title: Compulsory school attendance and excusal grounds
headings.reviewNote: Requires regular attendance for children ages seven to compulsory age and enrolled five-to-seven-year-olds, with excusal grounds for incapacity, legal employment at fourteen or older, parental drop request for ages five to seven, or documented mental or behavioral health concerns (source footnote notes 'chapters' in original rolls).

headings.title: Curriculum autonomy for nonpublic, home, and FPE schools
headings.reviewNote: Protects religious-doctrine curriculum choices and prohibits state departments or agencies from dictating any statewide curriculum for private, parochial, parish, home, or FPE schools.

headings.title: Statutory definition of school year duration
headings.reviewNote: Defines school year as beginning on the first day of July and ending on the thirtieth day of June following.

headings.title: Compulsory attendance age and metropolitan resolutions
headings.reviewNote: Defines compulsory attendance age as seventeen years or sixteen completed credits, authorizing metropolitan boards to adjust ages.

headings.title: Definition of completed credit towards graduation
headings.reviewNote: Defines a completed credit towards high school graduation for home and FPE schools as one hundred or more hours of instruction.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 167.031 governing compulsory school attendance requirements, curriculum autonomy, school years, and graduation credits.

headings.title: Reporting fifteen or more absences to children's division
headings.reviewNote: Requires school districts in cities not within a county to report students under age seventeen accumulating fifteen or more absences in a school year to the children's division within ten business days.

headings.title: Children's division parental notice and educational neglect
headings.reviewNote: Requires the children's division to notify parents of fifteen or more absences and potential section 210.145 educational neglect review regardless of parental approval of the absences.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.034 governing truancy reporting to the children's division in cities not within a county.

headings.title: Part-time school attendance for employed minors
headings.reviewNote: Requires parents of employed children under seventeen to compel attendance at district part-time classes for at least four hours weekly.

headings.title: Part-time attendance for minors without elementary completion
headings.reviewNote: Requires children under eighteen who have not completed the elementary school course or its equivalent and do not attend day school regularly to attend part-time classes at least four hours weekly.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.051 governing compulsory attendance requirements for part-time schools and classes.

headings.title: Establishment and assignment to special truant schools
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school boards in districts of ten thousand or more inhabitants to establish truant day schools and compel student attendance.

headings.title: Parental schools for juvenile wards and city or county support
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes boards to establish parental schools for resident children committed by a juvenile court under section 211.181, with ten dollars monthly paid from the city or county treasury.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.091 governing the establishment of truant day schools and juvenile court parental schools.

headings.title: Law enforcement notice of specified pupil offenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires prosecutors, juvenile officers, and law enforcement authorities to notify superintendents when charges, indictments, or section 211.031(1) petitions allege any of twenty-three enumerated offenses (source footnotes note transfers of sections 566.040 and 566.070).

headings.title: Oral and written notification timelines and dispositions
headings.reviewNote: Requires notification within twenty-four hours of charges without victim names, followed by disposition notices within two business days.

headings.title: Confidential sharing with staff and service limits
headings.reviewNote: Requires superintendents or designees to report received information in confidence to need-to-know staff, bars using it as the sole basis to deny educational services without seeking an injunction, and permits alternative-environment services.

headings.title: Superintendent notice of suspension to juvenile court
headings.reviewNote: Directs superintendents to notify juvenile or family court divisions upon suspensions exceeding ten days or expulsions of court wards.

headings.title: Superintendent consultant role in juvenile court proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes superintendents or designees to serve as consultants at juvenile dispositional proceedings involving pupil academic treatment plans.

headings.title: Forwarding written notifications upon pupil transfer
headings.reviewNote: Requires superintendents or designees to forward written subsection 2 notifications to the new district upon a pupil's transfer and upon any subsequent transfer.

headings.title: Inclusion of charter, private, and parochial schools
headings.reviewNote: Extends definitions of school and superintendent under this section to charter, private, and parochial schools and chief officers.

headings.title: Civil immunity for good faith reporting
headings.reviewNote: Grants civil immunity to school superintendents and employees who report disciplinary and charge information in good faith.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsection headings for 167.115 governing law enforcement notifications of specified pupil offenses, confidentiality, transfers, and immunity.

headings.title: Principal reporting of school assaults to police
headings.reviewNote: Requires principals to immediately report school assaults and sexual offenses to local law enforcement and superintendents, subject to agreements.

headings.title: Principal reporting of controlled substances and weapons
headings.reviewNote: Requires principals to immediately report pupil possession of controlled substances or weapons on school grounds or buses to law enforcement.

headings.title: Teacher duty to report incidents to principal
headings.reviewNote: Requires teachers to immediately report school assaults, weapons, or controlled substances discovered on school property to principals.

headings.title: Reporting agreements and referrals for young pupils
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes reporting agreements with law enforcement and referrals to the children's division rather than police for pupils under eleven.

headings.title: Employee duty to inform administrators of offenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires school employees becoming aware of reportable offenses to immediately notify administrators to make the required reports.

headings.title: Civil immunity for good faith reporting
headings.reviewNote: Provides civil immunity to school employees and officials providing incident information to law enforcement in good faith.

headings.title: Penalties for willful neglect of reporting duties
headings.reviewNote: Subjects school employees willfully neglecting or refusing reporting duties under this section to statutory penalties under section 162.091.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsection headings for 167.117 governing mandatory reporting of school assaults, weapons, and controlled substances to law enforcement.

headings.title: Juvenile officer notice of judicial custody status
headings.reviewNote: Requires juvenile officers or children's division employees to notify school districts when a child under judicial custody pursuant to section 211.031(3) is enrolling or an enrolled child is taken into judicial custody.

headings.title: Notification timeline and physical force descriptions
headings.reviewNote: Requires notice within five days of custody describing physical force conduct with intent to cause serious bodily harm without victim names.

headings.title: Superintendent confidential sharing and service protections
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes confidential sharing with school staff for discipline and counseling, prohibiting entry in permanent records or denial of services.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.122 governing juvenile officer notices to schools regarding children under judicial custody.

headings.title: Superintendent request for active juvenile case notification
headings.reviewNote: Requires juvenile officers or children's division staff to notify superintendents upon request when active cases exist regarding enrolled children.

headings.title: Five-day notification timeline and conduct description
headings.reviewNote: Requires notification within five days of requests describing case conduct and dates while protecting non-child victim identities.

headings.title: Confidential employee sharing and record restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Requires superintendents or designees to report received information in confidence to need-to-know staff for good order, discipline, intervention, or counseling, barring permanent record inclusion or sole-basis denial of educational services.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.123 governing school superintendent requests for juvenile case information and record safeguards.

headings.title: Commissioner hardship assignment criteria and driving distances
headings.reviewNote: Defines attendance center and requires the commissioner of education or designee, upon proper application in specified counties and villages, to assign eligible pupils and siblings to a closer receiving district when driving-distance and class-size conditions are met.

headings.title: Application priorities, continuing assignments, and eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Establishes application order priorities, continuation until grade completion, and public school attendance eligibility prerequisites.

headings.title: Sending district tuition liability and parental differences
headings.reviewNote: Requires sending districts to pay pro rata tuition costs and requires parents to pay tuition differences exceeding resident rates.

headings.title: Transportation route alterations not required
headings.reviewNote: Provides that receiving school districts are not required to alter transportation routes to accommodate hardship assigned pupils.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 167.125 governing commissioner hardship assignments of students to closer neighboring school districts.

headings.title: Right to educational services for placed or admitted children
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees educational services and bars denial of admission to appropriate public, special district, or state board programs for children admitted to mental health facilities or placed across districts by agencies, courts, or physician orders, while preserving agency or court authority to procure services.

headings.title: Domiciliary district responsibility for local tax effort
headings.reviewNote: Requires non-special domiciliary districts to pay an amount equal to average per-child local tax effort and special school districts to pay an amount not exceeding average domiciliary local tax efforts.

headings.title: Written voucher payments and state aid deductions
headings.reviewNote: Establishes ninety-day voucher payment timelines and authorizes state department deductions from state aid for delinquent payments.

headings.title: State excess cost funding for state-placed children
headings.reviewNote: Requires state department payment of excess per-pupil educational costs for children placed by state agencies or courts.

headings.title: Institutional authority to enroll resident children
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes residential institutions caring for juveniles to enroll children in local district or special district educational programs.

headings.title: Contractual admissions for out-of-state institutional children
headings.reviewNote: Permits contractual school admission of out-of-state resident children residing in local facilities without financial burden on Missouri.

headings.title: Definition of child domicile and public service rights
headings.reviewNote: Defines domicile as the district where child would have been educated and affirms rights to gratuitous public educational services.

headings.title: Inclusion in serving district average daily attendance
headings.reviewNote: Includes children receiving educational services in the average daily attendance of the serving district for state aid distribution.

headings.title: State payments in lieu of local tax effort
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department payments directly to serving districts in lieu of local tax effort for court or agency-placed children.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsection headings for 167.126 governing educational costs, local tax effort vouchers, and state aid for institutionalized children.

headings.title: Prohibition on aggregating facility and district pupil data
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the department from aggregating regularly enrolled pupil data with data from children residing in court-ordered group homes or institutions for neglected or delinquent children in MSIP reports.

headings.title: Federal compliance and separate educational agency reporting
headings.reviewNote: Maintains federal educational service duties while requiring state reports to treat neglected and delinquent facilities as separate agencies.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.128 governing the disaggregation of student data from facilities for neglected or delinquent children.

headings.title: Tuition and transportation duties of non-high school districts
headings.reviewNote: Requires districts not maintaining high schools through twelfth grade to pay tuition and provide transportation to accredited high schools.

headings.title: Per-pupil tuition calculation formula and state board review
headings.reviewNote: Establishes grade level grouping per-pupil tuition cost formula and provides for final state board resolution of tuition disputes.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.131 governing tuition and transportation duties of districts not maintaining a high school through twelfth grade.

headings.title: Definitions of transfer districts and adequacy target
headings.reviewNote: Defines receiving approved charter school, receiving district, sending district, and state adequacy target for transfer tuition.

headings.title: Calculation formula for transfer student tuition rates
headings.reviewNote: Limits transfer tuition paid by sending districts to the lesser of the receiving policy rate or adequacy target plus local tax effort.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.132 governing transfer tuition definitions and rate calculations for transfers under section 167.895.

headings.title: Discretionary admission of nonresident pupils and tuition
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school boards to admit nonresident pupils not entitled to free instruction and prescribe tuition fees subject to statutory exceptions.

headings.title: Tuition-free attendance for orphan and unsupported children
headings.reviewNote: Permits orphan children, children with one living parent, and children whose parents do not contribute to their support, ages six to twenty and unable to pay tuition, to attend school tuition-free where they have a permanent or temporary home.

headings.title: Tuition tax credits and property owner attendance options
headings.reviewNote: Provides property tax credits on tuition and allows owners of agricultural or residential property paying school taxes to enroll children.

headings.title: Notification procedures for agricultural land school choice
headings.reviewNote: Specifies June thirtieth written notice deadlines for agricultural landowners exercising options to send children to public schools across districts.

headings.title: Tuition attendance for children of school employees
headings.reviewNote: Requires specified charter-county districts with thirteen thousand to fifteen thousand pupils to allow nonresident children of district teachers or regular employees to attend upon tuition payment.

headings.title: Local policy for nonresident contractor and employee children
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes boards to adopt policies admitting children of school contractors and regular employees tuition-free with resident ADA status.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 167.151 governing nonresident pupil admissions, property tax credits, employee child policies, and tuition rules.

headings.title: Board authority for pupil suspension or expulsion
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school boards to suspend or expel pupils for conduct prejudicial to discipline, immediate threat removals, and hearing procedures.

headings.title: Suspension of pupils charged with felony offenses
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school boards to suspend pupils charged with, convicted of, or pleading guilty to felony criminal violations after notice and hearing.

headings.title: Good-faith effort for parental presence and due process
headings.reviewNote: Requires good-faith efforts to ensure parental presence and guarantees appropriate due process and trial de novo in circuit court.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.161 governing school board authority for pupil suspensions, expulsions, felony removals, and due process.

headings.title: Educational duty and alternative education program costs
headings.reviewNote: Affirms state and parental educational duties during suspension or expulsion, encourages in-school suspension alternatives, and sets local tax effort voucher payments and ninety-day state aid deductions (source footnote notes 'of this section' does not appear in original rolls).

headings.title: District contracting for alternative education services
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school districts to contract with political subdivisions, public agencies, not-for-profit organizations, or private agencies for alternative education services for disruptive students, with or without a section 167.335 grant application.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.164 governing educational duties during suspensions, alternative education voucher payments, and district contracting authority.

headings.title: Prohibition on student strip searches by school personnel
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits public and charter school employees and volunteers from conducting student strip searches, reserving authority to law enforcement.

headings.title: Emergency exception for imminent physical threats
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school employee strip searches only when police are unavailable and a student reasonably poses an imminent weapon or explosive threat.

headings.title: Exclusions from definition of strip search
headings.reviewNote: Excludes clothing removal for abuse investigations, medical attention, health services, and medical screenings from strip search definitions.

headings.title: Mandatory parental notification of student strip search
headings.reviewNote: Requires school districts to attempt to notify parents or guardians as soon as possible after a student is strip searched.

headings.title: Mandatory employee suspension without pay for violations
headings.reviewNote: Directs immediate unpaid suspension of public or charter school employees violating strip search prohibitions pending hearings.

headings.title: Definition of school employee under search provisions
headings.reviewNote: Defines employee under strip search provisions to include all temporary, part-time, and full-time school workers.

headings.title: Protection for nondisruptive emblems, insignia, and garments
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits school employees, volunteers, board members, and administrators from directing students to remove any emblem, insignia, or garment, including religious ones, worn in a manner that does not promote disruptive behavior.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsection headings for 167.166 governing prohibitions on student strip searches, exceptions, penalties, and nondisruptive emblem or garment protections.

headings.title: Prohibition on mandatory student radio frequency identification
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits school districts from requiring students to use radio frequency identification devices to track student locations or transmit data.

headings.title: Definition of radio frequency identification technology
headings.reviewNote: Defines radio frequency identification technology as wireless systems using electromagnetic signals to transmit data without physical contact.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.168 governing prohibitions on mandatory radio frequency student tracking identification devices.

headings.title: Summary suspension authority of principals and superintendents
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes summary suspensions up to ten days by principals and one hundred eighty days by superintendents, with board appeal procedures.

headings.title: Mandatory procedural due process requirements before suspension
headings.reviewNote: Requires notice of charges, factual explanation, and opportunity to respond before suspension, with stay of suspension pending appeal.

headings.title: Mandatory conference and restrictions on violent offenders
headings.reviewNote: Mandates conferences before readmitting pupils suspended over ten days for violence, barring regular readmission for enumerated felony crimes.

headings.title: Review conference for pupils suspended from other districts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes review conferences to evaluate out-of-district suspensions and determine whether equivalent conduct warrants exclusion.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 167.171 governing summary suspensions, procedural due process protections, and readmission conferences.

headings.title: Department rules governing required childhood immunizations
headings.reviewNote: Directs department of health and senior services to promulgate rules governing mandatory immunizations for children attending schools.

headings.title: Unlawful school attendance without required immunization evidence
headings.reviewNote: Makes it unlawful for students to attend school without immunization evidence and unlawful for parents to neglect required immunizations.

headings.title: Religious and medical exemptions from immunization
headings.reviewNote: Exempts children from immunization mandates upon written parental objection for religious beliefs or licensed physician medical certification.

headings.title: Superintendent immunization records and noncompliance reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires school superintendents to maintain immunization records for all enrolled pupils and report noncompliant parents to health department.

headings.title: Immunization administration, public expense, and fluoride
headings.reviewNote: Permits licensed physicians or supervised persons to administer immunizations, requires public-expense immunization when parents cannot pay, and authorizes treating physicians to administer dental fluoride treatments.

headings.title: State and federal funding for vaccine purchases
headings.reviewNote: Directs general revenue and federal fund appropriations to the health department for administering programs and purchasing vaccines.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and administrative nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Subjects immunization rules to chapter 536 administrative procedures, specifying invalidity of rules upon unconstitutional review powers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsection headings for 167.181 governing childhood immunization mandates, school attendance bars, exemptions, and public expense coverage.

headings.title: Department brochure on human papillomavirus and prevention
headings.reviewNote: Requires health department to develop parental brochures on HPV, cervical cancer risk factors, immunizations, and pap smears.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Subjects rules promulgated under this section to chapter 536 administrative procedures and nonseverability requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.182 governing informational brochures on human papillomavirus and cervical cancer for parents.

headings.title: Authorized disclosure of student immunization records
headings.reviewNote: Permits disclosing and exchanging childhood immunization records without written parental release to public agencies, school and child care health records staff, caregivers of state-custody children, and health care professionals.

headings.title: Civil damages liability for unauthorized record release
headings.reviewNote: Imposes civil damages liability on authorized persons who disclose confidential childhood immunization information for unauthorized purposes.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.183 governing disclosure of childhood immunization records and civil liability for unauthorized release.

headings.title: Acceptance of National School Lunch Act provisions
headings.reviewNote: Accepts the provisions and federal funds of the National School Lunch Act for state disbursement.

headings.title: Establishment of state treasury school lunch fund
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the School Lunch Fund within the state treasury for deposit of federal school lunch program moneys.

headings.title: State board of education administrative cooperation
headings.reviewNote: Designates the state board of education as the state educational agency to cooperate with the Secretary of Agriculture in program administration.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.201 governing acceptance of the National School Lunch Act and state lunch fund administration.

headings.title: Mandatory district policy on allergy prevention and response
headings.reviewNote: Requires school districts to adopt policies addressing potentially deadly food-borne allergies, staff roles, and confidentiality.

headings.title: Department development of model allergy policies
headings.reviewNote: Directs department of elementary and secondary education to develop model food allergy prevention policies in cooperation with associations.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.208 governing district food allergy prevention policies and department model policy development.

headings.title: Urban school lunch facility manager appointment and bonds
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes urban school boards to designate lunch managers, require surety bonds, mandate accurate accounting, and require annual reports.

headings.title: Deposit and security of lunch facility receipts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes board designation of secured depositories and check signers for lunch receipts, relieving district treasurers of custody.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.221 governing urban district school lunch facility managers, accounting, and depositories.

headings.title: High school postsecondary course option programs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes public high schools to offer postsecondary course options in cooperation with public and private colleges and universities.

headings.title: Resident district average daily attendance counting
headings.reviewNote: Directs resident school districts to continue counting pupils in average daily attendance while attending postsecondary courses.

headings.title: Resident student status for two-year college aid
headings.reviewNote: Deems high school pupils enrolled in two-year colleges under course options to be resident students for two-year college state aid.

headings.title: College course fee agreements and payments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes colleges and universities to charge reasonable fees paid by resident districts or pupils pursuant to local agreements.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 167.223 governing high school postsecondary course options, state aid, and college fees.

headings.title: Definitions of Braille and visually impaired students
headings.reviewNote: Defines Braille and student with visual impairments for statutory instruction provisions.

headings.title: Mandatory Braille instruction in individualized education plans
headings.reviewNote: Requires Braille reading and writing instruction in individualized education plans unless evaluations determine it inappropriate.

headings.title: Competency standards and specifications in education plans
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that Braille instruction must enable peer-level communication, requiring implementation details, start dates, and competency goals in IEPs.

headings.title: Teacher Braille competency certification standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires certified teachers of blind children to demonstrate Braille competence under National Library Service standards.

headings.title: Title and definitions under the BRITE Act
headings.reviewNote: Establishes title as the BRITE Act and defines accessible assistive technology, adequate instruction, and blind students.

headings.title: BRITE Act Braille presumption and plan requirements
headings.reviewNote: Establishes federal IDEA Braille presumption and requires detailed evaluation findings, implementation, and 504 plan accommodations.

headings.title: Instruction in expanded core curriculum
headings.reviewNote: Mandates instruction in expanded core curriculum to support blind and visually impaired students in the general education curriculum.

headings.title: Mandatory assistive technology instruction and IEP terms
headings.reviewNote: Requires assistive technology instruction in IEPs, detailing assessment findings, implementation, frequency, and competency benchmarks.

headings.title: Orientation and mobility instruction and evaluations
headings.reviewNote: Requires orientation and mobility instruction in IEPs or IFSPs unless determined inappropriate, requires 504 plan consideration, and mandates certified NBPCB/NOMC or ACVREP/COMS evaluations across daytime, nighttime, home, school, and community settings.

headings.title: Educator and specialist certification requirements
headings.reviewNote: Establishes certification and renewal credentials for educators hired to teach Braille, accessible assistive technology, and orientation and mobility.

headings.title: LEA service delivery, consent, and transportation duties
headings.reviewNote: Requires LEAs to comply with IDEA, ADA Title II, and the Rehabilitation Act including during emergencies, verify contractor certifications, allow daytime and nighttime orientation and mobility instruction, optionally require annual parental consent for off-hours or off-site instruction, and provide or reimburse transportation.

headings.title: Eye report costs, Section 508 compliance, and access
headings.reviewNote: Requires LEAs to pay for required eye reports without delaying eligibility evaluations, comply with U.S. Access Board Section 508 standards for electronic and information technology, and adopt nonvisual accessibility policies.

headings.title: School year applicability of section subsections
headings.reviewNote: Provides that subsections 1 to 4 apply in school years ending before July 1, 2022, and subsections 5 to 12 apply in school year 2022-23 and all subsequent school years.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 13 subsection headings for 167.225 governing Braille instruction, teacher certification, the BRITE Act, assistive technology, orientation and mobility, LEA duties, and school-year applicability.

headings.title: Nonresident pupil summer school attendance authorization
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes pupils to attend summer school in other public school districts if accepted, restricting enrollment to one district per summer.

headings.title: Resident status for summer school state aid
headings.reviewNote: Deems pupils attending nonresident summer programs to be residents of the attending district for summer term state aid.

headings.title: Inter-district cooperation and contractual summer services
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes public school districts to cooperate in utilizing faculty and resources and contract for summer school services.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.227 governing nonresident summer school attendance, state aid residence status, and district cooperation.

headings.title: Mandatory transportation distances, state aid, and tax elections
headings.reviewNote: Requires transportation for pupils over three and one-half miles, provides state aid for one mile, and authorizes tax elections for closer pupils.

headings.title: Statutory ballot form for pupil transportation tax
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the official ballot proposition format for voter approval of additional property taxes for under-one-mile pupil transportation.

headings.title: Discretionary transportation funded by parent payments
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school boards to transport non-eligible pupils if parents contractually agree in writing to pay full actual costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.231 governing pupil transportation mileage thresholds, state aid, tax levy elections, and parent-paid services.

headings.title: Proposition to rescind transportation tax and service
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes seven-director school boards to submit voter propositions rescinding tax levies and transportation for pupils living under one mile.

headings.title: Statutory ballot form for transportation tax rescission
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes the official ballot form for voter approval of rescinding under-one-mile transportation requirements and tax levies.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.232 governing voter rescission of tax levies for under-one-mile pupil transportation.

headings.title: Resident district duty to transport tuition pupils
headings.reviewNote: Requires districts of residence to provide transportation for pupils whose tuition they must pay under section 167.131 or who are assigned under section 167.121, except as otherwise provided in this section.

headings.title: Transportation limited to accredited or designated districts
headings.reviewNote: Restricts transportation duties to accredited school districts or those specifically designated by the board of education of residence.

headings.title: Transportation duties for transfer students and charter schools
headings.reviewNote: Defines approved charter school and requires districts of residence to transport pupils covered by section 167.895 only to accredited districts or approved charter schools designated by the department or its designee.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.241 governing resident district transportation duties for tuition students and approved charter schools.

headings.title: State aid eligibility for early childhood at-risk programs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes state aid for half-day programs serving developmentally delayed and at-risk children ages three and four in full-day kindergarten districts.

headings.title: State board approval and distribution of preschool aid
headings.reviewNote: Directs the state board of education to approve early childhood programs and distribute corresponding state aid.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.260 governing state aid eligibility for preschool and at-risk programs in full-day kindergarten districts.

headings.title: Program for teacher assistants in early elementary grades
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the K-3 teacher assistant program, defines teacher assistant, and sets eligibility criteria including breakfast, forty-percent free/reduced lunch, and a section 167.268 reading intervention plan (source footnote notes change to 'reading success plan' in 2020).

headings.title: District application, supplement amounts, and assignment limits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes financial supplements of three thousand dollars per assistant, restricting assignments to regular kindergarten through third grades.

headings.title: State board rules governing qualifications and award methods
headings.reviewNote: Directs state board to promulgate rules establishing assistant qualifications, classroom pupil minimums, and funding award procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.263 governing state financial supplements for teacher assistants in early elementary grades.

headings.title: School counselor program for grades K-9 and eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a state financial supplement program for school counselors in grades kindergarten through nine and sets enrollment, breakfast, and forty-percent free/reduced lunch eligibility criteria.

headings.title: District application, supplement limits, and counseling duties
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes financial supplements up to ten thousand dollars per counselor and requires direct counseling activities during funded school hours.

headings.title: State board rules governing counselor qualifications and funding
headings.reviewNote: Directs state board to promulgate rules establishing additional qualifications, application procedures, and salary schedule supplement amounts.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.265 governing state financial supplements for elementary and middle school guidance counselors.

headings.title: Establishment of academic and career counseling programs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school districts and charter schools to establish academic and career counseling programs in cooperation with parents and communities.

headings.title: State board rules and administrative nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs state board to promulgate implementation rules subject to chapter 536 administrative procedures and nonseverability clauses.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.266 governing district academic and career counseling programs and state recognition.

headings.title: Mandatory district policy on reading success plans
headings.reviewNote: Requires school districts and charter schools to maintain reading success plan policies and provide parents with home reading suggestions.

headings.title: Department guidelines for reading improvement and dyslexia
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to develop guidelines on reading proficiency measures, remediation strategies, dyslexia screening, and exemptions.

headings.title: Mandatory intensive reading instruction for students
headings.reviewNote: Requires school districts and charter schools to provide intensive reading instruction pursuant to statutory requirements in section 167.645.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.268 governing reading success plan policies, department guidelines, and intensive reading instruction.

headings.title: Dropout prevention programs and additional state aid
headings.reviewNote: Encourages local school districts to offer specialized courses for at-risk pupils with additional state financial assistance.

headings.title: State reimbursement rate per full-time teacher
headings.reviewNote: Sets state reimbursement rates for approved dropout prevention courses at eight thousand eighty-three dollars per full-time teacher.

headings.title: Alternative education for pregnant teens and teen mothers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes state aid subject to appropriation, supplemental services, multi-district consortia, contracts, and optional tuition waivers for alternative education programs serving pregnant teens and teen mothers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.270 governing specialized dropout prevention courses, state reimbursement rates, and programs for pregnant teens and teen mothers.

headings.title: Mandatory reporting of high school dropouts to hotline
headings.reviewNote: Requires secondary schools to report students sixteen or older who drop out to the state literacy hotline for adult education referral.

headings.title: Monthly public electronic reports omitting student identities
headings.reviewNote: Requires monthly electronic publication of dropout reports on the department website, strictly excluding identifying student information.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.275 governing secondary school dropout reports to the state literacy hotline and monthly publications.

headings.title: Competitive grants for dropout prevention support services
headings.reviewNote: Directs the state board to award competitive grants to higher education institutions, consortia, and nonprofits for dropout prevention services.

headings.title: Mandatory elements in grant funding applications
headings.reviewNote: Specifies required application components including at-risk identification systems, volunteer and parent involvement, and continuity of services.

headings.title: Priority criteria for awarding dropout prevention grants
headings.reviewNote: Establishes funding priorities for applications replicating proven models, demonstrating institutional commitment, and ensuring graduation.

headings.title: Consideration of institutional and community matching funds
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the state board to consider private gifts, federal aid, and local matching funds contributed by applicants in grant awards.

headings.title: Service locations for nonpublic school pupils
headings.reviewNote: Requires dropout prevention services for nonpublic school pupils to be provided at sites other than sectarian nonpublic schools.

headings.title: Authorized compensatory and support service activities
headings.reviewNote: Specifies allowable service uses including skills assessment, tutoring, personal counseling, family home visits, and staff development.

headings.title: Allowable program administrative and personnel costs
headings.reviewNote: Lists allowable expenditure categories including personnel salaries, student stipends, transportation, materials, and administration.

headings.title: State board rules governing grant program administration
headings.reviewNote: Directs the state board of education to promulgate all rules and regulations necessary for implementing the grant program.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsection headings for 167.280 governing competitive grant awards for dropout prevention support services to at-risk pupils.

headings.title: Grants for alternative education for disruptive students
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a state grant program for school districts providing alternative education for students with demonstrated disruptive behavior.

headings.title: Joint applications, vocational centers, and rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Encourages joint regional applications and area vocational center participation, directing the state board to promulgate rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.335 governing grant assistance for alternative education programs serving disruptive students.

headings.title: Title of Read to be Ready Program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes statutory title as the Read to be Ready Program for sections 167.340 to 167.346.

headings.title: Additional average daily attendance for reading instruction
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes counting students receiving early elementary reading improvement instruction outside school hours for additional state aid attendance.

headings.title: Authorized reading improvement instruction methods
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes summer school, smaller class sizes, computer resources, specialists, teacher training, tutoring, and phonics instruction.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.340 governing the Read to be Ready Program, extra state aid attendance, and instruction methods.

headings.title: Four-year competitive matching grant program for reading
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a four-year matching grant program to defray district and building costs of reading assessments and intervention training.

headings.title: Application requirements for reading assessment grants
headings.reviewNote: Requires grant applications to describe existing programs, demonstrate need for improved methods, and explain integration of assessments.

headings.title: Mid-grant progress report for years three and four funding
headings.reviewNote: Requires grantees to show student reading improvement after year two and report third-grade communication arts assessment progress to receive funding for years three and four.

headings.title: Post-grant reimbursement of district match for progress
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department, upon demonstration of significant improvement from appropriated funds, to reimburse a district's match and directs rulemaking to define significant progress.

headings.title: Four-year grant renewal and one-time match reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Allows grants to be renewed for an additional four-year term based in part on first-grant results and limits match reimbursement to a one-time payment.

headings.title: Inclusion of vision- or hearing-impaired students
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in the act prohibits including vision- or hearing-impaired students in reading improvement grant programs or considering applications focused on them (source footnote notes H.B. 889, 1999).

headings.title: Geographic grant distribution and fund reallocation
headings.reviewNote: Requires equal grant distribution within geographic areas proportionate to student population while permitting department reallocation when an area has insufficient eligible applications.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 7 subsection headings for 167.343 governing four-year reading matching grants, applications, mid-grant progress, match reimbursement, renewal, sensory-impaired inclusion, and geographic allocation.

headings.title: Recommended K-3 reading assessments list and updates
headings.reviewNote: Directs the state board to develop a research-based list of recommended K-3 reading assessments by July 1, 2000 as a non-mandatory guideline and directs the department to update it from grant results.

headings.title: Guidelines applying reading assessments to instruction
headings.reviewNote: Directs the state board of education to develop guidelines applying reading assessment results to instructional programs and teacher and administrator training for below-grade-level readers.

headings.title: Department rulemaking for Read to be Ready provisions
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of elementary and secondary education to adopt rules implementing sections 167.340 to 167.346.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Subjects rules created under this section to chapter 536 and section 536.028 and makes rulemaking authority and rules after August 28, 1999 nonseverable from legislative review powers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 167.346 governing recommended K-3 reading assessments, instructional guidelines, department rulemaking, and chapter 536 nonseverability.

headings.title: Definitions for school children health services sections
headings.reviewNote: Defines family practitioner, most accessible care, school age children, school children health services, and service area for sections 167.600 to 167.621.

headings.title: Nonseverability of school children health sections
headings.reviewNote: Provides that sections 167.600 to 167.621 are not severable from each other.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.600 governing statutory definitions and nonseverability for sections 167.600 to 167.621.

headings.title: School election to function as Medicaid provider
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes public schools and districts to elect to serve as Medicaid providers and deliver early screening or primary care to children.

headings.title: Written agreement determining scope of health services
headings.reviewNote: Directs social services department and participating districts to determine the scope of EPSDT and primary care services by written agreement.

headings.title: Provision of EPSDT services by district personnel
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school district personnel to provide early periodic screening, diagnosis, and treatment health services directly to students.

headings.title: Contracts with community health centers and clinics
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes participating districts to contract with qualified health centers, health departments, clinics, and physicians for primary care.

headings.title: District employment of medical personnel under standing orders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes direct employment of medical professionals under physician standing orders if unable to contract with community providers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 167.606 governing school Medicaid provider elections, scope of services, and healthcare provider contracts.

headings.title: Annual social services assessment of participating districts
headings.reviewNote: Directs the social services director to determine annual assessments for participating districts to underwrite service costs.

headings.title: Intergovernmental transfer of state aid for federal match
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes transferring district state aid disbursements to the health initiatives fund to capture federal matching Medicaid funds.

headings.title: General revenue support for disproportionate eligible children
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of social services to commit general revenue funds and permits provider arrangements when a participating Medicaid-provider school or district has a disproportionate number of eligible resident children excluded from section 163.081 funding.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.609 governing district Medicaid assessments, intergovernmental fund transfers, and general revenue support for disproportionate eligible children.

headings.title: Establishment and composition of school health advisory committee
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school districts to establish advisory committees of parents, teachers, medical professionals, and students to monitor services.

headings.title: Parental consent form and affirmative contraceptive referral
headings.reviewNote: Requires parental consent checklists before providing health services, barring contraceptive referrals without affirmative parent selection.

headings.title: Identification of family practitioner and medical histories
headings.reviewNote: Directs school staff to identify family practitioners for students, provide practitioner lists, and update medical histories annually.

headings.title: Prohibition on school provision of contraceptives
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits school personnel or their agents from providing contraceptive devices or contraceptive drugs and requires referring students seeking them to the designated family practitioner.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 167.611 governing school health advisory committees, parental consent, family doctors, and contraceptive bans.

headings.title: Parental authorization required before providing services
headings.reviewNote: Requires health providers to obtain parental or guardian authorization pursuant to section 431.061 before rendering health services.

headings.title: Protection for unqualified staff refusing medical tasks
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits requiring unqualified employees to administer medical services, shielding them from discipline, while protecting first aid.

headings.title: Civil immunity for qualified staff administering medication
headings.reviewNote: Grants civil immunity to qualified school employees administering medication or medical services in good faith under standard practices.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.621 governing parental authorization for health services, employee protections, and qualified staff immunity.

headings.title: Short title of Will's Law
headings.reviewNote: Provides that section 167.625 shall be known and may be cited as Will's Law.

headings.title: Definitions for Will's Law epilepsy care provisions
headings.reviewNote: Defines individualized emergency health care plan, individualized health care plan, parent, school, school employee, and student with epilepsy or a seizure disorder.

headings.title: Individualized health and emergency plans for seizure care
headings.reviewNote: Requires parents seeking seizure care to notify the school and provide annual written authorization, requires school nurses to develop and annually update individualized plans, and lists required and optional plan contents.

headings.title: Biennial school employee epilepsy and seizure care training
headings.reviewNote: Requires school nurses or administrators to coordinate seizure care and ensure biennial training of all school employees through a DHSS-approved course from a Missouri-based organization.

headings.title: Parental release for medical information sharing and HIPAA
headings.reviewNote: Requires school nurses or administrators to obtain a parental release authorizing medical information sharing among health care providers and school employees without violating HIPAA.

headings.title: Good faith immunity for school employees and nurses
headings.reviewNote: Grants civil and professional licensing immunity to school employees and nurses acting in good faith without gross negligence.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 167.625 (Will's Law) governing epilepsy and seizure disorder definitions, individualized care plans, biennial staff training, medical releases, and good-faith immunity.

headings.title: Definitions of epinephrine systems and self-administration
headings.reviewNote: Defines epinephrine delivery system, medication, and self-administration for school chronic health condition management.

headings.title: Mandatory authorization for pupil medication self-administration
headings.reviewNote: Requires school boards to authorize student possession and self-administration of asthma and anaphylaxis medication upon doctor and parent plans.

headings.title: Scope and annual renewal of self-administration authorization
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes medication possession at school and sponsored events, requiring annual authorization renewal by parents each school year.

headings.title: Emergency backup supply of duplicate prescription medication
headings.reviewNote: Requires keeping duplicate prescription medications in an accessible school location for immediate staff access during emergencies.

headings.title: Accessibility of treatment plans during school emergencies
headings.reviewNote: Requires keeping treatment plans and liability statements on file in locations easily accessible during health emergencies.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 167.627 governing pupil self-administration of asthma and anaphylaxis medications and emergency supplies.

headings.title: Definition of epinephrine delivery system
headings.reviewNote: Incorporates the statutory definition of epinephrine delivery system from section 167.627 for school supply authorizations.

headings.title: Board authorization for school nurse supply of epinephrine
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school boards to permit licensed school nurses to maintain an adequate supply of epinephrine delivery systems at school.

headings.title: Prescription requirements designating school district as patient
headings.reviewNote: Requires healthcare provider prescriptions naming the school district as patient and nurse as recipient, filled at licensed pharmacies.

headings.title: Discretionary emergency administration and civil immunity
headings.reviewNote: Gives school nurses, trained contracted agents, and trained supervised employees discretion to administer epinephrine for suspected life-threatening anaphylaxis, with civil immunity for trained employees under section 167.624 and for trained contracted agents.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 167.630 governing district supplies of epinephrine delivery systems and trained staff administration.

headings.title: Board authorization for school nurse asthma medication supply
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school boards to permit licensed school nurses to maintain a supply of asthma-related rescue medications at school.

headings.title: Prescription requirements designating school district as patient
headings.reviewNote: Requires prescriptions for school asthma rescue medication designating the district as patient, filled at licensed pharmacies.

headings.title: Discretionary emergency administration and civil immunity
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes nurses and trained staff to administer asthma medication during acute episodes, extending statutory civil immunity.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.635 governing district supplies of asthma rescue medications and trained employee administration.

headings.title: District student promotion policy and remediation conditions
headings.reviewNote: Requires school districts to adopt a student promotion policy that may require remediation as a condition of promotion and may require parental home-based tutorial commitments, with IEPs governing parental involvement for students with disabilities.

headings.title: Remediation program methods and special education plans
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes summer school and out-of-school remediation methods, requiring instruction for disabled students to conform to IEPs.

headings.title: Counting extra remediation hours in average daily attendance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes school districts providing remediation outside regular school days to count extra instructional hours in state aid attendance.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 167.640 governing student promotion policies, remedial education programs, and additional attendance counting.

headings.title: Mandatory reading assessments and reading success plans
headings.reviewNote: Requires reading assessments in kindergarten through grade three and new students in grades one through five, providing reading success plans.

headings.title: Annual written parental notice of reading deficiencies
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual written notice to parents of students with reading deficiencies detailing current services, proposed remediation, and home strategies.

headings.title: Parental notice of summer reading program opportunities
headings.reviewNote: Directs schools offering summer reading programs to notify parents of students exhibiting substantial reading deficiencies of attendance options.

headings.title: Third-grade promotion or retention consultation with parents
headings.reviewNote: Requires personal consultation with parents and formulation of remediation action plans before deciding to retain third-grade pupils.

headings.title: Mandatory school duties for deficient and dyslexic readers
headings.reviewNote: Requires districts and charter schools to provide free intensive reading supports, systematic evidence-based dyslexia instruction, progress notices at least four times per year, and parent-guided home reading plans.

headings.title: Criteria for intensive reading development initiatives
headings.reviewNote: Mandates regular school-hour reading instruction covering phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, and comprehension.

headings.title: Reporting reading interventions and assessment data to department
headings.reviewNote: Requires school districts and charter schools to report implemented reading interventions and kindergarten through fifth grade assessment data.

headings.title: Comprehensive school improvement plans and teacher development
headings.reviewNote: Requires reading proficiency strategies in school improvement plans and professional development for teachers on evidence-based reading strategies.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsection headings for 167.645 governing student reading assessments, reading success plans, parental notices, and third-grade retention.

headings.title: Establishment of after-school retreat reading grant program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a competitive grant program within the department for school district after-school reading and student assessment programs.

headings.title: State appropriation and grant award procedures
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department grant awards from state appropriations and establishes proration procedures if available funds are insufficient.

headings.title: Creation of grant program fund in state treasury
headings.reviewNote: Creates the After-School Retreat Reading and Assessment Grant Program Fund in the state treasury, administered by the department, with interest credited and biennium balances exempt from transfer to general revenue under section 33.080.

headings.title: Chapter 536 compliance for promulgated rules
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no rule or portion of a rule promulgated under this section takes effect unless promulgated pursuant to chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 167.680 governing the After-School Retreat Reading and Assessment Grant Program, pro rata awards, state treasury fund, and chapter 536 rulemaking.

headings.title: State board policy encouraging parent and family involvement
headings.reviewNote: Directs the state board of education, in consultation with districts, personnel, and parents, to adopt a policy by December 1, 2005 encouraging parent and family involvement and to consider it in district consultations and public interactions.

headings.title: Required elements and goals of state involvement policy
headings.reviewNote: Specifies six required elements and goals for the state board policy, including home-school communication, responsible parenting support, open school visitation, parent partnership in decisions, and community resources.

headings.title: Mandatory school district parent involvement policies
headings.reviewNote: Requires each school board, in consultation with the state board, personnel, and parents, to adopt parent and family involvement policies by March 1, 2006 consistent with subsections 1 and 2.

headings.title: Annual review and amendment of involvement policies
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state board and each school district board of trustees to review and amend their parent and family involvement policies at least once each year.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 167.700 governing state board and school district parent and family involvement policies, required elements, and annual review.

headings.title: Definitions of physical activity, education, and recess
headings.reviewNote: Defines moderate physical activity, physical education, and recess for section 167.720.

headings.title: Elementary physical activity, recess, and middle school option
headings.reviewNote: Requires elementary moderate physical activity (150 minutes per five-day week or 30 minutes daily) and 20-minute daily recess beginning 2010-11, requires annual commissioner fitness recognition, permits 225 weekly minutes in middle schools, and specifies qualifying activities.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.720 governing physical education, moderate physical activity, and recess definitions and school requirements.

headings.title: Brain Injury Prevention Act title and DHSS guidelines
headings.reviewNote: Names the section the Interscholastic Youth Sports Brain Injury Prevention Act and directs DHSS, by December 31, 2011, to work with school board, activities, and brain injury organizations to promulgate concussion education rules, guidelines, and forms.

headings.title: Annual concussion information sheet and parent signature
headings.reviewNote: Requires each school district annually to distribute a concussion and brain injury information sheet that must be signed by a parent or guardian and submitted before athletic practice or competition.

headings.title: Removal of youth athletes for suspected concussion
headings.reviewNote: Requires removing a youth athlete suspected of sustaining a concussion or brain injury in practice or a game from competition at that time and for no less than twenty-four hours.

headings.title: Health care provider evaluation and written return clearance
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a removed youth athlete from returning to competition until evaluated by a licensed health care provider trained in concussion evaluation and management with written clearance.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Subjects rules created under this section to chapter 536 and section 536.028 and makes rulemaking authority and rules after August 28, 2011 nonseverable from legislative review powers.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 167.765 governing the Interscholastic Youth Sports Brain Injury Prevention Act, parent forms, 24-hour removal, medical clearance, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Annual athletic organization report on concussions
headings.reviewNote: Requires statewide athletic organizations with a public school district member to publish and distribute an annual report on concussions and head injuries to legislative education committees, starting by January 31, 2012, and make it available to districts and parents.

headings.title: Membership prohibition for noncompliant organizations
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits public schools from being members of any statewide athletic organization that fails to comply with the subsection 1 reporting requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 167.775 governing annual concussion and head injury reports by statewide athletic organizations and membership prohibitions for noncompliance.

headings.title: Definitions for FPE, home, and virtual student participation
headings.reviewNote: Defines athletics, event or activity, fine arts activities, FPE school, full-time equivalent student, home school, and integrated cocurricular activities for section 167.790.

headings.title: Prohibition on membership in noncompliant associations
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits a school district or charter school from being a member of or remitting funds to any statewide activities association that would cause a violation of this section.

headings.title: Prohibition on barring participation or requiring classes
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits districts and charter schools from barring FPE, home, or virtual FTE students from trying out or participating in resident events or requiring class attendance, except under subsections 4 and 5.

headings.title: Permissible instructional components for specific activities
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that districts and charter schools may require integral instructional components for fine arts activities, career and technical student organizations, and integrated cocurricular activities.

headings.title: Equal disciplinary and attendance policies for participants
headings.reviewNote: Permits disciplinary or attendance policies for required coursework, rehearsals, or practices, requires equal application to all participants, and prohibits separate policies for FPE, home, or virtual FTE students.

headings.title: Twelve-month ineligibility after ineligible disenrollment
headings.reviewNote: Makes students who disenroll while academically or disciplinarily ineligible to attend an FPE, home, or virtual school ineligible for public or charter events in that district or charter school for twelve calendar months.

headings.title: Parental oversight of FPE and home school academic standards
headings.reviewNote: Makes the parent or legal guardian providing primary instruction responsible for overseeing academic standards directly relating to an FPE or home school student's participation.

headings.title: Eligibility requirements and confidentiality of records
headings.reviewNote: Requires residency proof under section 167.020, a sports physical, equal conduct standards, and equal financial requirements, and bars disclosing created or retained records except for federal or state law compliance.

headings.title: Exclusion of other gatherings and local policy discretion
headings.reviewNote: Excludes unrelated extracurricular gatherings or special occasions from 'event or activity' and leaves districts and charter schools free to include or exclude FPE, home, or virtual FTE students.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsection headings for 167.790 governing FPE, home, and virtual FTE student participation in public and charter school events and activities, policies, and eligibility.

headings.title: Definitions of activities association and department
headings.reviewNote: Defines activities association, department, and public school for interscholastic athletic appeals and governance provisions.

headings.title: Establishment and gubernatorial appointment of commission
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the five-member Interscholastic Athletic Oversight Commission appointed by the governor with senate advice and consent.

headings.title: Jurisdiction over student athletic transfer and contest appeals
headings.reviewNote: Directs the oversight commission to hear only athletic-transfer eligibility and contest-procedure appeals, stating both that it hears appeals after association exhaustion and that an appealing party may file directly without first exhausting the association's process.

headings.title: Commission recommendations for association rule changes
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the oversight commission to recommend changes to activities association rules and regulatory procedures.

headings.title: Annual legislative report by activities associations
headings.reviewNote: Requires an activities association to prepare and present an annual report to designated house and senate committees within the first thirty days of the legislative session.

headings.title: Administrative staffing and procedural appeals rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to provide administrative support and promulgate procedural rules and timelines for commission hearings.
